text: BOFA WARNS AI BOOM COULD FOLLOW HISTORIC BUST CYCLES Bank of America warns that the AI investment boom is showing signs of a classic capital-cycle risk: surging spending, intensifying competition and falling prices. Hyperscaler capital expenditure expectations have jumped from $330 billion to $1 trillion, equivalent to roughly 3% of U.S. GDP. Meanwhile, AI token prices have fallen around 50% since summer, raising concerns that growing usage may not translate into sufficient revenue. The key risk: AI technology could succeed while investors suffer from overinvestment and declining returns.

text: IMF Pledges Support as Iraq Seeks Emergency Financial Assistance Iraq has approached the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for a new financial program as the US-Israel war with Iran disrupts oil exports and squeezes government revenue. IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva pledged “firm” support, including financing and policy assistance, though the size and terms of the program remain undecided. The IMF forecasts Iraq’s economy will contract 16% in 2026 before rebounding 19% in 2027. The crisis has also prompted Iraq to devalue its currency by 13% against the dollar as disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz hit oil shipments. The IMF is simultaneously advancing discussions on potential support for Lebanon, highlighting mounting economic pressures across the Middle East.
